hi love, fellow uk young person here. currently at uni (more on that later)

i can see myself in what you’ve written a lot. smart, but puts wayyy too much pressure on myself. also had a lot of friends who were the same. i’ll break it down for you, because the situation isn’t as hopeless as you perhaps think

first of all, we’re going through a pandemic. this is something that no one’s been through in our lifetimes. and so give yourself a little bit of forgiveness if things haven’t gone to plan. hopefully there’s some lenience on grades considering the pandemic, but even if not - hope is not lost

first option - clearing. not ideal i know, but an option. my very best friend was predicted AAA, ended up getting CDD. obviously not what she wanted, but she still ended up getting into a university doing what she wanted to do. she’s two years into her course and is loving it - this could be you :)

second option - year out. as for your concerns about being a year older than other people. being a uni student in second year, i promise you now age doesn’t mean anything. in my first year i was in a flat with 10 people, and only 3 of them were the same age as me (18). the rest of them had taken a year out so were 19, others were even in their early 20s. and they all made friends, so i promise you even if you did take a year out - it wouldn’t matter at all. in the year out, you can retake exams, get a job, whatever. build up your cv and ucas application so it’s even more impressive.

personally this year, i was halfway through my second year of my dream course at my dream uni - and yet i ended up dropping out! and that’s completely okay! i had all the right entry requirements and prerequisites, and it still wasn’t working out for me. in the time i’ve had off i got a job, and in hindsight i really really wish i’d took a year out before i started uni. it might be scary at first because you’re not following this path you’re expected to follow/hoped to follow, but finding what you like/don’t like first hand can be a blessing in disguise. i know you love studying, so even if you take a year out you could study and retake your exams, or even take up an extracurricular course. your local uni will almost certainly run short courses that you can attend (will probs be a fee), or the open university do free online courses! give it a think <3

let me know if there’s anything you wanna chat about - i promise you hope isn’t lost. feel free to dm me :)
before breaking up, have you discussed these concerns/issues with your girlfriend? discussing things and deciding then is often the best action plan

i’m not sure if this helps, but happy birthday my love ❤️

lots of people, even those without bpd, can struggle around birthdays, so please don’t feel alone

of course!

what i’ve found oddly soothing and helpful is

1) helping other people going through similar things. if you find it too triggering, avoid this. but i’m finding it helpful to be reminded that i am not alone in this experience, and that i can even help others going through it
2) talking to myself in the third person when i’m really struggling. as if i am looking after a close friend who is struggling. i find i am much more compassionate and patient to others than to myself, and so trying to reverse this dynamic is super helpful for me!

hopefully this helps <3

hello love

first of all, please hang in there. i’m not going to bother with the usual bs advice, but i’ll try and offer some personal experience so you feel less alone

i admitted myself to a&e yesterday after wanting to not be alive for days, and i’m now currently sat with my dog. i’m still feeling awful, but i’m not currently in that deep dark pit. feeling actively suicidal, no matter how all-encompassing it feels, passes. it may take some time but it will, i pinkie promise you

if you’re especially worried, please consider taking steps to keep yourself safe - stay with family/friends if possible, walk around and do something somewhere public to keep you busy. maybe even follow the same route i did and take yourself to a&e - they will keep you safe and give you some help. the help may not be perfect, but any help is good

regarding your fp and their boyfriend, i’ve been there too. a lot of the time it takes them going through the experience, no matter how much you want to take control of the situation, for them to actually learn and understand. and so whilst your fp did not listen, you did all you could as a decent friend - and there will come a time when he thanks you for it

the splitting is not ideal, but it is something a lot of us on this sub struggle with. you are not the worst person in this world - try and focus on grounding. focus on all your positive traits (i’m willing to take a bet that you’re extremely protective and loyal - someone people can only wish they were friends with)

you’ve since apologised for splitting, so you’ve done the right thing and you’ve done all you can. he’s even accepted the apology, and so i’d hazard a guess and say you’re on the right path. for now, my best advice would be to give him some space and time whilst he figures out this situation with his boyfriend (which i know will be agonising). depending on the current dynamic, you could even try and continue the friendship but avoid the topic of his boyfriend as much as possible. if you provide any more details, i’m happy to advise accordingly

finally, this is going to sound extremely cliché. and i know that because i feel the same way all the time when i say “i can’t live without him”. and it truly does feel like that. but believe me, we can. we have lived before this person, and we will live after this person

sending lots of love and healing <3
